main_result: There is a finitely generated group G_D and a square integer matrix A over Z[G_D] (size 2d+1), invertible over Q[G_D], whose Fuglede–Kadison determinant is q^{-θ} with q=2^k>1 and θ=(1/3)(2/3)^{|S|}>0. So 0<det<1, and the integral (1/n)τ_n(log T_A*T_A) equals -2θ log q/(2d+1)<0. This is a square counterexample to the group-ring determinant inequality ∫log t dμ_A ≥ 0. The construction is conditional on a cited characteristic-two existence theorem: a finite field K_2 of characteristic two, a finitely generated H_2, and a_2,b_2 in K_2[H_2] with a_2b_2=1≠b_2a_2.
proof_strategy: Start from the cited one-sided inverse pair a_2,b_2 over a char-2 field and map it into Mat_d(F_2[H_2]) by a unital injective ring map, which yields X,Y with XY=I and an idempotent C=I-YX≠0 (Lemma binary). Build a rational idempotent p in Z[1/3][G_D], with G_D a sum of cyclic C_3 coordinates semidirectly multiplied by H_2, that has identity coefficient θ>0 and kills the binary defect mod 2, so P=diag(I_d,p) has trace d+θ and reduction factoring through d columns (Proposition separation). Lemma lift lifts that factorization modulo q=2^k using a finite geometric series in a corner ring, and Lemma integral builds an integral block matrix A with rational inverse whose Schur complement is J=-q^{-1}P-(I-P). The shear path L_xBR_x preserves the trace of log(M*M) because its tracial logarithmic derivative vanishes (Lemmas logderivative and shears), so log det A equals log det B=(r-τ(P))log q. I checked the block algebra, the Schur complement, the idempotent and vanishing identities psp=0, the trace θ computation, and the derivative formula in Lemma logderivative line by line and found no error. The only parts I could not check are the cited companion theorem and the cited Elek–Szabó statement.
hardest_part: The cited existence theorem (the characteristic-two companion, Theorem 1.1) is the load-bearing input: every later step is conditional on it, and I could not verify its construction or its claimed a_2b_2=1≠b_2a_2 over a finite field. Within the manuscript, the hardest checkable step was the reduction-mod-2 bookkeeping in Proposition separation (that p̄ h_0^{-1}C_ij p̄ = p̄ using psp=0 and the coefficient identity), but I did verify it. I also could not independently confirm the cited Elek–Szabó statement's exact hypotheses for the sofic corollary.

main_result: The manuscript claims a counterexample to the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture. It builds a finitely generated group G_D = (⊕_{h∈H_2} C_3) ⋊ H_2, where H_2 and a_2, b_2 come from an external theorem giving a finite characteristic-two field K_2 and a_2 b_2 = 1 ≠ b_2 a_2 in K_2[H_2]. It then gives a square integer matrix A of size 2d+1 (d = [K_2:F_2]), invertible over Q[G_D], with 0 < det_N(T_A) = q^{-θ} < 1, where θ = (1/3)(2/3)^{|S|} > 0 and q = 2^k ≡ 1 mod 3^{1+|S|}. The integral ∫ log t dμ_A equals −2θ log q/(2d+1) < 0, which is finite.
proof_strategy: Step 1 (Lemma binary): a char-2 scalar failure of direct finiteness is pushed through the regular representation of K_2 over F_2 to give X, Y over F_2[H_2] with XY = I, C = I − YX ≠ 0, and C idempotent with XC = 0 = CY. Step 2 (Proposition separation): a rational idempotent p = p_1 ∏_{s∈S}(1 − p_s), built from averaging projections on commuting C_3 coordinates, has psp = 0 for s ∈ S and identity coefficient θ; reducing mod 2 gives a factorization of diag(I_d, p̄) through d columns. Step 3 (Lemmas lift and integral): a Hensel-type geometric series in a corner ring lifts the factorization mod q = 2^k, and the block matrix A = [[qI, V],[U, q^{-1}(UV − P − q(I−P))]] is integral with Schur complement J = −q^{-1}P − (I−P). Step 4 (Lemmas logderivative, shears, Proposition criterion): the trace of log(M*M) along the path M(x) = L_x B R_x is constant, since the derivative is 2Re τ(M'M^{-1}) and the shear contributions are traceless; evaluating at x=0 gives τ(log B*B) = 2(r − τ(P)) log q. I re-derived the block products, the Schur complement, the conjugation identity psp = 0, the trace identities, and small test cases (trivial group, n=2,3) by hand and they were consistent. The only step I could not check myself is the external existence theorem that supplies K_2, H_2, a_2, b_2; the convention identifying T_A with the group-ring matrix is also only asserted.
hardest_part: The entire disproof rests on the cited companion theorem (Theorem 1.1 of CharacteristicTwo) producing a finite field K_2 of characteristic two, a finitely generated H_2, and a_2 b_2 = 1 ≠ b_2 a_2. The manuscript explicitly says it does not execute or check any instance, so I could not verify this input. Beyond that, the identification of the operator T_A on ℓ²(G)^n with the group-ring matrix A (left vs right action, via the inversion unitary) is asserted in one sentence and I could not confirm it from the text.

Without this the disproof is conditional on an unchecked external claim, and the reader cannot confirm that H_2 is finitely generated.

main_result: The manuscript claims a counterexample to the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture. It constructs a finitely generated group G_D = (⊕_{h∈H_2} C_3) ⋊ H_2 and a square integer matrix A of size 2d+1 over Z[G_D], invertible over Q[G_D], with Fuglede–Kadison determinant q^{-θ} where q=2^k, θ=(1/3)(2/3)^{|S|}>0, and q≡1 mod D. Hence 0<det<1 and ∫log t dμ_A(t) = -2θ log q/(2d+1) < 0. The construction starts from a cited existence theorem: a finite characteristic-two field K_2 and a finitely generated H_2 with a_2b_2=1≠b_2a_2 in K_2[H_2]. I checked the internal algebra and it holds: the idempotent p, the factorization of its mod-2 reduction through d columns, the Z-lift via the corner geometric series, the block-shear path M(x)=L_xBR_x, and the trace-invariance lemma (derivative of τ log(M*M) equals 2Re τ(M'M^{-1}), which has zero trace in the shear case). The determinant then equals q^{-θ}.
proof_strategy: Step 1 (Lemma binary, Prop separation): from the cited a_2,b_2 build binary matrices X,Y over F_2[H_2] with XY=I and C=I−YX a nonzero idempotent with XC=0, CY=0. Pick a nonzero coefficient of C and form the idempotent p = p_1 ∏_{s∈S}(1−p_s) from commuting order-3 coordinate idempotents, so that psp=0 for s∈S, [1]p=θ, and p̄ h_0^{-1}C_ij p̄ = p̄. Step 2 (Lemma lift): mod 2 the factorization P̄=uv through d columns is lifted to Z/2^k by the corner-ring geometric series Q=e+W+…+W^{k−1}, with W nilpotent because its entries are divisible by 2. Step 3 (Lemma integral): the block matrix A with B=diag(qI_r, J) and shears L_x, R_x gives an integral A with rational inverse, whose lower-right block is UV/q+J. Step 4 (Lemmas logderivative and shears, Prop criterion): the trace of log(M*M) is constant along the shear path, so it can be evaluated at x=0 where B*B is diagonal, giving log det = (r−τ_m(P)) log q. Step 5 (assembly): take r=d and τ_{d+1}(P)=d+θ to get log det = −θ log q. The external input is used only to produce the scalar pair.
hardest_part: The load-bearing premise is the cited companion theorem (Theorem input): a finite characteristic-two field, a finitely generated group, and a one-sided inverse in K_2[H_2]. The manuscript says it does not execute or verify any explicit instance and that the field is not asserted to be F_2. A one-sided inverse over a finite field would be a serious claim about direct finiteness, and I cannot check it. Separately, I could verify the internal algebra, but the normalization and the definition of T_A (left versus right action, and the inversion-unitary remark) are stated loosely, so the link between the matrix A and the operator whose determinant is computed is the part I trust least.
